title: An explanation of the hierarchy between the gravitational and particle mass scales

concept.text: Strings 2000 problem 9 (proposed by Matt Strassler): what physics explains the enormous disparity between the gravitational scale and the typical mass scale of the elementary particles? Sources given: https://preskill.caltech.edu/millennium.html ; https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v54.i10.14_2.online.pdf ; https://x.com/martinmbauer/status/1779906631003697211.

page.title: Resolution of the electroweak hierarchy problem
page.definition: An experimentally supported explanation of why the electroweak scale v, the Higgs field’s vacuum value of about 246 GeV, is only 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁷ of the unreduced Planck energy E_P = √(ħc⁵/G). The Standard Model fits v to observations. The full hierarchy problem asks what accounts for this separation all the way to the Planck scale. Stabilizing the Higgs sector up to an intermediate energy addresses the narrower little hierarchy problem.

goal.need: Higgs measurements test how particles acquire mass across three orders of magnitude in particle mass. Muon decay fixes the strength of the low-energy weak interaction to about 0.6 parts per million. Even an exact value would still be an input to the Standard Model. Explaining its origin would tell us what sets the mass scale of the W and Z bosons and how it coexists with much higher energies. If the mechanism changes Higgs interactions or predicts particles within reach, collider experiments could test those predictions.

figures.caption: The separation between electroweak and gravitational scales
figures.note: Using ħ = c = 1, v is calculated from CODATA's Fermi constant through v = (√2 G_F)^−1/2. The ratio is calculated. Parentheses give one standard uncertainty in the final digits.

completion.title: A validated physical mechanism quantitatively accounts for the electroweak–Planck hierarchy.
completion.criterion: A peer-reviewed physical explanation accounts for v/E_P ≈ 2.0 × 10^-17, using the unreduced Planck scale and units ħ = c = 1. The separation follows from specified dynamics, symmetry or selection conditions, with its dependence on free parameters and quantum corrections explicit. Independent measurements corroborate predictions that identify the proposed mechanism.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no model-independent completion test was found in the sources searched.
completion.basis: Strings 2000, P5 2023, NASEM 2025, PDG's Higgs review and Peskin's hierarchy review were searched for a solution criterion, a numerical fine-tuning cutoff and a validation protocol. None supplied a model-independent completion test. This fallback combines the stated demand for an explanation of the scale separation with experimental identification of its mechanism.

milestones.title: A proposed hierarchy mechanism's predicted new effect is observed with at least 5σ significance.
milestones.criterion: A new-particle signal or other effect predicted by a proposed hierarchy mechanism rejects the known-process hypothesis at a significance of at least 5σ. For a one-sided test of an excess, 5σ corresponds to p ≈ 2.87 × 10⁻⁷. The analysis accounts for systematic uncertainties and assesses the effect of searching across a range of signal hypotheses where applicable.

milestones.title: Measurements satisfy a proposed hierarchy mechanism's distinguishing parameter relations.
milestones.criterion: Independent measurements constrain the combinations of parameters in a proposed hierarchy mechanism’s distinguishing relations and satisfy those relations within the reported experimental and theoretical uncertainties. For a weakly coupled top-partner model, test the predicted cancellation using the measured masses of the top quark and its partners and their couplings to the Higgs boson, including the relative signs required by the sum rule.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback: searches of PDG, P5, NASEM and hierarchy reviews found no mechanism-independent validation threshold. Csáki and colleagues supply a specific sum-rule test for weakly coupled partner explanations, not a universal criterion.

milestones.title: Higgs production and decay rates constrain separate couplings to weak bosons and to fermions.
milestones.criterion: Fit two coupling modifiers jointly to measured Higgs production and decay rates. One modifier scales the couplings to both W and Z bosons, and the other scales the couplings to fermions. Use the benchmark with Standard Model loop contributions rescaled by those modifiers and no additional invisible or undetected decays. Report the joint constraint relative to the Standard Model point, where both modifiers equal one.
milestones.set_by: LHC Higgs Cross Section Working Group, Light Mass Higgs Subgroup, two-parameter benchmark in Table 4.

vector boson couplings are

not_found: No model-independent completion criterion or numerical fine-tuning acceptance threshold was found in the committee reports and hierarchy reviews searched.
No common experimental precision or universal sequence of milestones was found for the competing hierarchy explanations.
No estimate was found of the share of collider searches attributable specifically to the electroweak hierarchy problem.

results.finding: ATLAS observed a combined diphoton and four-lepton Higgs excess of approximately 10σ in its full 2015–2016 dataset. The briefing gives no event count or integrated luminosity.
results.quote: the statistical significance of the observed excess over the background prediction from the combination of the H→γγ and H→ZZ→4l channels is approximately 10σ and thus well beyond the 5σ threshold for a (re-)discovery.

results.finding: CMS observed H → WW production at 9.1σ in 35.9 fb⁻¹ of collision data, with 36,800 selected events across nine categories.
results.detail: The significance combines all categories at an assumed Higgs mass of 125.09 GeV. The combined cross section times branching fraction was 1.28 times the Standard Model prediction, with uncertainties of +0.18 and −0.17.
results.quote:
The observed signiﬁcance in the asymptotic approximation [68] of the Higgs boson
production for the combination of all categories is 9.1 s.d., to be compared with the expected
value of 7.1 s.d.
